report.summary: Checkout-service experienced a 1.6× increase in resident memory and repeated OutOfMemoryError and GC overhead limit warnings during the 3‑hour window.

likely_causes.title: Memory leak within checkout-service
likely_causes.rationale: Repeated OOM errors and high GC overhead indicate that the application is allocating memory that is not being released, causing the heap to fill.

supporting_evidence.detail: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space (4 occurrences between 11:53:46 and 12:14:46 UTC)
GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92% (16 occurrences between 10:59:46 and 12:14:46 UTC)

likely_causes.title: Insufficient JVM heap size configuration
likely_causes.rationale: Heap usage reached 92% and OOM errors occurred, suggesting the configured heap may be too small for the workload.

supporting_evidence.detail: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space (4 occurrences between 11:53:46 and 12:14:46 UTC)
GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92% (16 occurrences between 10:59:46 and 12:14:46 UTC)

next_steps: Collect and analyze heap dumps from the affected instances
Review recent code changes for new allocations or retained objects
Examine GC logs for patterns of sustained high usage
Consider increasing the JVM heap size or tuning GC settings
Monitor memory usage post‑remediation to confirm resolution
